structured_output.world_model:
W5 (contrarian), after E046. The tip is still E036 (5.314 s; seeds 0–2 at 0.7532).

1. Rebuild noise sets the floor. Commit 60645dd has read 0.7532, 0.7525 and 0.7497. Accuracy-neutral changes land between 0.7512 and 0.7549. I model each build plus seeds 0–2 as one draw, with an SD of about 0.2 pp around a population mean of about 0.7522–0.7530. That mean sits at or just under the 0.753 gate, so a neutral change passes only about 35–40% of the time. My 80% accuracy bands stay at about ±0.3 pp.

2. E046 broke two of my beliefs.
   - It saved 0.235 s over about 23 frozen steps, roughly 10 ms per step, which is about a third of a 32 px step. Group 2's backward FLOPs (about 2/3 of half the MACs) only partly explain that.
   - It held 0.7540 on seeds 0–2, so my claim that the end of the run is a sharp optimum, where any late change costs 0.2–0.4 pp, is weakened. Freezing parameters at an annealed LR (E028, E036, E046) is gentle. The changes that hurt were ones that altered the *objective* or the *averaging* (E025, E030, E032, E044).
   - Revised mechanism: annealing a parameter group to LR 0 and then freezing it leaves the Lookahead end-point almost unchanged. Changing what is averaged, or the loss surface, is what costs accuracy.

3. A mechanism nobody has named: per-step optimizer and launch cost is a large, hidden share of step time. Every freeze also removes Muon work for the frozen filters. That work is the norm, renorm, Newton-Schulz on bf16 matrices and the foreach copies, run as per-parameter small kernels that are launch- or bandwidth-bound. Both E028 (about 27% of a step for about 13% of FLOPs) and E046 saved more than FLOP accounting predicts. Freezing also removes wgrad, which is memory-bound on small maps. My model is: step time ≈ conv compute + a roughly fixed optimizer/elementwise tail of perhaps 25–35%. If that holds, the open levers are:
   - one fused or batched Newton-Schulz across same-shape filters (group-2 and group-3 convs 2 and 3 share a shape);
   - skipping the renorm on most steps;
   - folding the Lookahead lerp into the step graph.
   These are off the accuracy frontier. Muon applies no wd, and wd ×0.5 affected only the SGD groups (H1.5.4 is settled by reading the code). Newton-Schulz already runs 3 iterations.

4. Steps versus pixels. E045 (twice the steps at 20 px) gained nothing. The early phase is saturated, and batch dials are worth only their overhead.

5. Time is reproducible to about ±0.02 s. Pixel-based accounting predicts the resolution and step levers well, but it under-predicts backward truncation by about 1.5–2×. Group-1 conv1 is about 6% of MACs. With channels_last fp16 and Cin=24 (a multiple of 8), tensor cores already engage, so explicit padding to 32 should give ≤1% and could even be slower.

6. Strategy. A time-only lever is now kept only if it costs ≤0.05 pp. The best candidates are those that leave the trajectory bit-identical (optimizer overhead), plus staggered freezes with annealing. E046 was discarded despite 0.7540, presumably on its held-out read. I have not seen that number, and it is my biggest uncertainty.

Unsure:
- E046's 20-seed delta;
- whether the profiler shows the optimizer tail at ≥20% of a step;
- whether the PCIe judge penalizes bandwidth-bound levers;
- the true population mean of E036 (fresh seeds 13–22 read 0.7538).

forecasts.reason: Recipe is unchanged, so the numbers are rebuild noise. I expect conv1 to run below group 2's TFLOP/s but at under 10% of the step, with the larger surprise being the optimizer/elementwise tail. That makes H6.4.1 likely only half true.
About 5% fewer steps should cut time by about 5%, but the accuracy cost of roughly 0.1–0.15 pp sits on the frontier and inside the noise, so the ≤0.1 pp condition is hard to resolve.
Cin=24 is already a multiple of 8 in channels_last fp16, so tensor cores engage. Padding adds input bandwidth on 31×31 maps; expect a saving of 1% or less, not ≥2%.

cruxes: Why did E046 save about 10 ms per frozen step, roughly 1.5–2× its FLOP share? If the profiler shows the Muon, renorm, Lookahead and elementwise tail at ≥20% of a step, then fusing or batching Newton-Schulz across same-shape filters is a trajectory-identical lever worth several percent.

What was E046's 20-seed (13–32) delta against E036? If it is within 0.1 pp, annealed staggered freezes are nearly free and the cascade should be pushed further (for example group 2 from 85%, group 3's later convs). If it is ≤−0.2 pp, the frontier holds.
Does the profiler show Cin=24 conv1 at a materially lower TFLOP/s than group 2? This decides whether I073 is worth running at all.
